transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-17 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Shannon Lee (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Pelican Head of ML), Priya Rao (Pelican Infra Lead), Tom Willis (Pelican CTO)

Summary (auto): Discussed per-token economics, batching/caching levers and deployment models. Agreed to benchmark and share security docs.

00:00 Shannon: hey everyone thanks for joining good to meet you. um quick intros?
00:08 Alex: alex here head of ml at pelican, we run a few inference endpoints for research and production, we wanna cut cost and not sacri- sacrifice latency.
00:15 Priya: priya infra lead, we'll own any network bits, V P C stuff, sso and k m s keys.
00:20 Tom: tom cto, i'm mostly interested in costs and compliance.
00:26 Shannon: awesome. marco and i will run through cost levers; marco's our infra/se will cover batching, kv cache and dedicated sizing.
00:33 Marco: hi all, quick q to understand scale - alex, what's your monthly token volume and typical prompt/response lengths?
00:41 Alex: right now prod is around 15M tokens a month, peak qps ~25, avg prompt around 80 tokens and response 220 tokens so gen is heavier. we have some low-latency chat that needs p95 under 150ms ideally.
00:56 Marco: perfect. and any data residency or retention constraints?
01:00 Priya: must stay inside our vpc for some datasets, and keys need to be customer-managed in our KMS. SOC 2 is required for vendor.
01:10 Shannon: that's common. Redwood private and dedicated both support customer KMS and V P C peering; hosted can be used if you use our private plane option but you mentioned wanting customer keys?
01:22 Tom: yeah we prefer customer-managed keys and audit trails; hosted's black-box is tough. but open to dedicated if costs justify.
01:30 Marco: on cost - two main levers: per-token pricing + model selection, and operational levers like batching, KV/prefix cache, quantization and autoscaling behavior. we'll walk through impact estimates.
01:40 Marco: per-token: Redwood hosted list is X cents per input token and Y cents per output token for the open LLMs; for dedicated you get reserved capacity and a much lower per-token runtime cost but there's a monthly commit.
01:53 Alex: can you give a ballpark difference? dedicated versus hosted?
01:56 Marco: ballpark: for high sustained throughput, dedicated can be 40-65% lower per-token cost once you amortize the commit over usage; hosted is easier - you pay higher per-token but no commit. exact numbers depend on sequence length and batching.
02:12 Alex: ok that matches our intuition. batching helps a lot right? but we care about that 150ms p95 so we can't batch arbitrarily.
02:19 Marco: exactly - batching increases GPU utilization, so per-token cost drops, but latency increases. Redwood supports dynamic batching with latency SLOs; you can set a max latency threshold and the runtime will trade-off batching accordingly. we've seen 25-50% cost savings from smarter batching on chat workloads with 80-200 token sequences when you allow p95 up to ~200ms.
02:44 Priya: what about prefix or KV cache? we do a lot of repeated prefixes across calls for our assistant flows.
02:50 Marco: KV cache/prefix caching is one of the biggest wins - if 30-40% of tokens are repeated prefixes, effective billed tokens drop a lot because we avoid recomputing past context. Redwood's caching layer can be shared across routes or pinned to dedicated pools; hosted supports caching but retention windows differ.
03:10 Alex: are cache hits billed? like do you still pay for the output tokens?
03:14 Marco: you pay for the generated output tokens; you don't re-execute the prefix so compute cost drops. depending on config you may still have small overhead for fetching KV, but it's minimal.
03:25 Tom: curious about quantization. we run some models at fp16 now; can you do int8 or lower to reduce cost?
03:31 Marco: yes, Redwood supports quantized kernels for many open models; it reduces memory and per-token GPU compute. quality tradeoffs depend on model; we can recommend quant profiles per workload. for some tasks int8 is fine and lowers cost by ~20-30%.
03:46 Alex: ok good. network overhead and embedding costs? we also do embeddings for rerank- is that separate pricing?
03:53 Shannon: embeddings are priced separately as per-unit; we'll include embedding per-1k pricing in the sheet. rerank cost can be much smaller if you cache embeddings and only update periodically.
04:05 Priya: security - we need SOC2 + audit logs and SSO. does Redwood provide audit logs for Private and Dedicated?
04:12 Shannon: yes both provide audit logs; Private gives you full control and logs live in your cloud account. Dedicated has tenant isolation and audit trails; hosted provides logs but some customers prefer Private for compliance. we'll attach SOC2 report and security pack.
04:30 Alex: on cost modeling, can you send an example calc? e.g., we want to model 15M tokens with x% cache hits and batching improvements.
04:38 Marco: yes we'll send an example spreadsheet. sample calc fields: model cost per token, effective tokens after cache, batching multiplier (efficiency), commit amortization for Dedicated, and infra egress/network.
04:52 Tom: what's typical commit sizes? we don't want to overcommit.
04:56 Shannon: commitments are flexible - monthly or annual; we can model a small starter commit that buys lower compute unit rates and you can adjust. some customers do 3-6 month pilots with a reduced commit.
05:10 Priya: how do you handle autoscaling? spikes are common during market opens for us.
05:16 Marco: Dedicated pools have autoscale with burst capacity options; you can reserve baseline GPU capacity and allow bursts to hosted capacity or fallback model variants. that gives cost predictability while keeping availability.
05:30 Alex: fallback models - you mean lower-cost model variants when primary is saturated? any quality gating?
05:35 Marco: yes you can configure fallback policies: e.g., route to a smaller quantized model, or route to hosted endpoints if dedicated is at capacity. rollouts have canary and A/B so you can test quality before failover.
05:50 Tom: latency numbers - can you hit p95 150ms for 300 token responses?
05:55 Marco: depends on model and hardware; for sequence lengths up to ~300 tokens with optimized kernels on A100/4090-ish hardware, p95 150ms is tight but achievable with small batch sizes and warmed KV. for very low-latency workloads we recommend Dedicated pinned pools with prewarmed KV.
06:15 Priya: what's the integration work to use our KMS? any agent required?
06:20 Shannon: typically we use cloud-native KMS integration (AWS KMS/GCP KMS) via customer-managed keys and IAM roles. for on-prem we have HSM connectors. Marco can follow up with the detailed network diagram.
06:34 Alex: what's the expected ops burden if we choose Private? we have a small infra team.
06:38 Marco: Private needs more ops from your side - it's customer-managed control plane and networking; Redwood provides automation and support, but Dedicated (managed by Redwood) is lower ops. tradeoff is stronger data isolation for Private.
06:55 Priya: any SLA differences?
06:58 Shannon: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime/latency targets depending on contract; Hosted has standard per-route SLOs; Private SLA is negotiated as part of the enterprise package.
07:10 Alex: ok next steps - would like benchmark and pricing.
07:14 Shannon: we'll send the security pack and a pricing spreadsheet today, marco will prepare a benchmark checklist and sample prompts. can we schedule a 60-min benchmark next week?
07:23 Tom: yes next wed works for us.
07:26 Shannon: great i'll send calendar invite and the initial docs.
07:30 Alex: any competitive concerns? some teams are leaning to Anthropic for safety but cost is higher; internal self-host is cheaper but ops heavy.
07:40 Marco: noted. we'll include head-to-head notes.
07:45 Shannon: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with action items.
07:50 Tom: thanks, bye.

End transcript.
